To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cysteine dioxygenase (CDO) knockout mouse has a phenotype that is characterized by excess cysteine, cystine, and hydrogen sulfide (H2S)/hydrosulfide (HS(-)) production in nonhepatically derived tissues.

cysteine dioxygenase knockout mice are viable and develop a phenotype that includes pancreatic and lung toxicity and that the phenotype is associated with increased levels of cysteine and H2S/ HS(-) in nonhepatically-derived tissues.

the KO mouse exhibits altered cysteine and cysteine metabolite metabolism in the nonhepatic organs and tissues that results in excess production of H2S and HS(-) and evidence of pancreatic (islet cell toxicity) and lung toxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of cysteine dioxygenase (CDO) in the regulation of the cysteine metabolism.
the development and application of novel methods and techniques for the study of the structure, dynamics and function of biomolecules and biomolecular systems at the molecular level.

the study of the mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis and progression of the chronic inflammatory process in the pancreas and the role of the pancreatic microenvironment in the development of pancreatic cancer.
